title: CRS Defense Primer: Emerging Technologies
summary: The CRS primer synthesizes the defense implications of artificial intelligence, lethal autonomous systems, hypersonic weapons, directed energy, biotechnology, and quantum technology. It emphasizes maturity, operational concepts, ethics, oversight, authorization, appropriations, and the future of warfare.
key_findings: The technologies differ materially in maturity, operational use, and governance questions.
AI and autonomy create speed and data advantages but also bias, assurance, and human-control risks.
Quantum, biotechnology, hypersonics, and directed energy create distinct sensing, materials, safety, and infrastructure dependencies.
why_it_matters: The primer provides a nonpartisan synthesis that helps keep technology claims bounded by maturity and oversight context.
ftfn_relevance: Supports cross-topic comparison without collapsing unlike technologies into a single readiness claim.
Adds congressional oversight and appropriations questions to the research-to-deployment stack.
evidence_limits: The primer is a high-level synthesis and does not replace program-specific technical evidence.
Fast-moving fields may have changed since the January 2026 update.
